topPRs.title: rust: update reth to v2.3.0
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
## Description

Updates the reth git pin from `7680d6d8` to the upstream **v2.3.0 release tag** (`9384bc53`), picking up 158 upstream commits, and syncs the shared dependency pins across all three Cargo workspaces (main, op-rbuilder, rollup-boost):

- `revm` 38 → 40.0.3 (and the revm-* family)
- `alloy-evm` 0.34 → 0.36
- `alloy-eip7928` 0.3.7 → 0.4.0, `revm-inspectors` 0.39 → 0.40.1
- published reth-core crates (`reth-primitives-traits`, `reth-codecs`, `reth-rpc-traits`, `reth-zstd-compressors`) 0.3.1 → 0.4.1 — reth now consumes these from crates.io, so a mismatch produces duplicate-crate type errors

The previous pin was an unmerged-PR commit carrying an engine-deadlock fix; upstream closed that PR as superseded by [#24875](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/24875), which is in v2.3.0, so nothing is lost and the pin moves from an unauditable PR commit to a release tag.

### API adaptations

- **op-revm**: revm 40 reworked the `Gas` reservoir API — `Gas::new_spent_with_reservoir` replaces `new_spent`, `state_gas_spent` is now signed, `Handler::last_frame_result` gained an `original_reservoir` parameter, and the failure path recovers the pre-tx reservoir via `saturating_add_signed`. The override mirrors the new upstream default (including the EIP-8037 failed-CREATE reservoir refund, inert until Amsterdam) while preserving the OP deposit/Regolith branches.
- **alloy-op-evm**: the state hook moved from `BlockExecutor`/`SystemCaller` into the revm `State` DB and now fires on commit; the manual `on_state`/`try_on_state_with` calls and `set_state_hook` impl are removed. Post-block balance increments still reach the hook via `increment_balances` → `commit_iter`.
- `PrecompileProvider::warm_addresses` returns `&AddressSet`; `EvmFactory::Error` GAT bound is now `DBErrorMarker`; `BuildPendingEnv::build_pending_env` gained a `BlockOverrides` parameter; `PayloadConfig` gained `parent_block_info`; `TransactionPool` gained `retain_contains`/`blob_store`; reth-tracing init returns `TracingGuards`; `Account::original_info` is private.

Also extends `rust/UPDATING-RETH.md` with the gotchas this bump surfaced: the four-manifest rev pin (vendored op-rbuilder/rollup-boost workspaces), the published reth-core crate version sync (with the duplicate-crate failure signature), and the slot-preimage layout revisit step.

## Tests

- `cargo check --workspace --tests` clean in all three workspaces; `just lint` (fmt + clippy + docs, `-D warnings`) green.
- `just test-unit`: 2478 passed, 11 skipped; op-rbuilder workspace: 108 passed.
- AI review (code + security) approved; both consensus-adjacent changes (gas reservoir handling, state-hook relocation) were verified line-by-line against the upstream implementations in the adopted dependency versions.
- The EIP-8037/reservoir paths in `op-revm::last_frame_result` are covered by four new unit tests (`FrameResult::Create` with Amsterdam enabled/disabled, successful CREATE, and signed reservoir recovery from negative `state_gas_spent`); each was verified red against a deliberately broken variant (refill disabled; unsigned recovery arithmetic) and green against the real code.

topPRs.title: feat(op-chain-ops): validate L2 genesis allocs in production generation
topPRs.author: lumoswiz
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Adds `genesis.CheckL2GenesisAllocs`, a structural validator for generated L2 genesis allocs. It checks EIP-1967 admin and impl slot coherence and rejects any account that is not a known predeploy, implementation, precompile, preinstall, or allowed EOA. Runs in both production generation paths: the op-deployer pipeline and interopgen. Also extends Go `DevAccounts` to match the 30 accounts L2Genesis funds.

**Tests**

- `TestCheckL2GenesisAllocs`: unit tests, happy path plus mutations.
- `TestL2GenesisAllocsInvariants`: op-deployer integration test asserting predeploy invariants across five alloc modes. Interop predeploys and the L1Block `INTEROP` runtime flag are asserted inactive in every mode, including the modes that set `UseInterop` (#20812). Regression oracle for #21342.
- `TestEndToEndBootstrapApply` covers the pipeline wiring. op-e2e interop tests cover interopgen.

**Additional context**

Part of #20903. The proxy admin owner is allowed as a plain EOA because artifacts predating #21339 leave it with a bumped nonce. The pipeline allowance is permanent. The oracle test's entry will be dropped once #21339 merges, so prefer merging after #21339.

Interop-at-genesis is deliberately not covered: no mode schedules it, and whether op-deployer should support that configuration at all is being raised with the interop team separately.

**Metadata**

- Fixes #21340

topPRs.title: op-core/types: add DepositTx, PostExecTx and Receipt types
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
## Description

Part of the op-geth decoupling (#20257); closes #20262. Creates `op-core/types` (imported as `optypes`) with the OP-Stack-specific transaction and receipt types, per §1–§3 of [docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md):

- **`DepositTx`** — standalone RLP type matching op-geth's wire format (`0x7E || RLP(struct)`), with `MarshalBinary` / `UnmarshalDepositTx`. No dependency on go-ethereum's `TxData` interface.
- **`PostExecTx`** — standalone type for the SDM post-exec transaction (`0x7D || data`, opaque-bytes payload, not RLP), with `MarshalBinary` / `UnmarshalPostExecTx`. Like op-geth, decoding rejects an empty payload (typed-tx envelopes of `len <= 1` are unparseable).
- **Free-function helpers** replacing op-geth's `Transaction` methods: `IsDepositTx`, `SourceHash`, `Mint`, `IsSystemTx`, `IsPostExecTx`. The accessors re-encode the tx and decode via `UnmarshalDepositTx`, so they work on upstream `*types.Transaction` after the cutover.
- **`Receipt`** — embeds `types.Receipt` and adds the six OP Stack L1-cost/operator-fee fields with JSON names verbatim from op-geth. Custom `UnmarshalJSON` decodes the wire's hex encoding via `hexutil`; a matching `MarshalJSON` merges the fields back in so the type round-trips (the promoted upstream marshaler would silently drop them).

**Differential tests** (to be removed at the final cutover) assert byte-for-byte equality of both tx encodings against op-geth, compare helper outputs against op-geth's `Transaction` methods on round-tripped txs, and check receipt JSON decode/re-encode against op-geth's marshaler. Notable behavior pinned down by the tests: a nil `Mint` round-trips to `0` through the wire encoding — in op-geth too.

Also updates the decoupling doc for `PostExecTx` (§1 + summary table).

Call-site swaps follow in #20263.

## Tests

- `go test ./op-core/types/...` — new unit + differential tests.
- `just lint-go` clean.

## Additional context

No production code uses the new package yet; consumers migrate in #20263.

topPRs.title: feat(op-core): add op-core/fees (L1 cost + operator-fee math)
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Creates **`op-core/fees`** (imported as `opfees`), a standalone, pure-math home for the OP-Stack L1 data-availability cost and operator-fee calculations, ported from op-geth's `core/types/rollup_cost.go`. This is part of the op-geth decoupling (§4 of [`docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md)).

It also fixes **#17817**: `op-service/txinclude` budgeted operator fees with the Isthmus formula, which under-budgets on Jovian chains.

## What's in the package
- `RollupCostData`, `NewRollupCostData`, `TxRollupCostData`, `EstimatedDASize`
- L1 cost: `L1CostBedrock`, `NewL1CostFuncEcotone`, `NewL1CostFuncFjord` (all return the public `L1CostFunc`)
- Operator fee: `OperatorCostIsthmus`, `OperatorCostJovian`
- `FlzCompressLen` (in `fastlz.go`) and the exported Fjord regression constants

Dependencies: standard library + go-ethereum `core/types`/`params` only. No dependency on `op-core/types`, so the two packages stay cycle-free siblings.

## Notes for reviewers
- **`TxRollupCostData` uses `tx.MarshalBinary()`, not `tx.Data()`** (which the original #20261 sketch had). The DA cost is computed over the full encoded transaction, with deposits short-circuited to empty — matching op-geth's `(*Transaction).RollupCostData()`. A parity test (`TestTxRollupCostDataParity`) enforces this across legacy/dynamic-fee/blob/deposit txs.
- **Scope of legacy funcs:** the pre-Fjord cost funcs are used by e2e tests (`op-e2e/.../system_config_test.go` → `L1Cost`, `op-e2e/system/fees/fees_test.go` → the state dispatchers). This PR ports the **pure-math** ones (`L1CostBedrock`, `NewL1CostFuncEcotone`). The state-reading dispatchers (`NewL1CostFunc`/`NewOperatorCostFunc`) are intentionally **not** ported — post-decoupling they're test-only (the L2 STF is op-reth/kona) and would couple this pure-math package to `op-core/params` + a `StateGetter`. They belong with the Phase-4 e2e test migration.
- **#17817 fix — always-Jovian.** Both the estimate (`OperatorCostOracle.OPCost`) and the actual-cost refund (`TxBudget.AfterIncluded`) now use `OperatorCostJovian`. Jovian is exact on Jovian chains (all production chains) and `>=` the Isthmus result for any inputs, so on a (nonexistent-in-prod) pre-Jovian chain it only over-reserves budget — never under-budgets. `IsthmusCostOracle` was renamed to `OperatorCostOracle` accordingly.
- All cost functions are pinned to op-geth's own reference values (Fjord Solidity-parity `105484`, Ecotone `960900`, Isthmus/Jovian operator `1256417826611659930`/`1256650673615173860`).

## Verification
`go build`, `go vet`, `go test`, and `gofmt` all pass for `op-core/fees` and `op-service/txinclude`.

> The repo's custom `golangci-lint` could not be run locally: the linter binary (built with go1.24) panics type-checking the `core/types` dependency graph, which now contains files declaring go1.25/1.26. This is a pre-existing local toolchain mismatch — it crashes identically on untouched `core/types`-importing packages (e.g. `op-batcher/batcher`) and is unrelated to this change.

Fixes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20261
Fixes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/17817

topPRs.title: docs(op-challenger): dispute-game-investigator skill + investigation guide
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
A read-only **dispute-game-investigator** skill/agent for diagnosing fault dispute games — challenger disagreements, excessive moves, self-contradiction, proposal validity, and the bond outcome.

- `docs/ai/dispute-game-investigation.md` — the playbook: identify actors → enumerate (`list-games`/`list-claims --format json`) → canonical output root (`op-chain-ops check-output-root`/`check-super-root`, EL-only) → classify claims (clamped to the safe head at the game's `l1Head`) → diagnose the responsible op-node → honest-actor non-counter rule (`solver.go`) → bond outcome (`FaultDisputeGame.sol`).
- `.claude/skills/...` + `.claude/agents/...` entrypoints; registered in `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`.
- `op-challenger/scripts/{check-game-block-hashes,game-proposal-outputs}.sh` — chain-agnostic helpers (curl + python3).

Distilled from the 2026-06-09 ink-mainnet incident (challenger disputing valid proposals due to an incomplete safe-head DB behind a load balancer). Draft.
